newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: VOTE says NZ Electoral Commission ads misleading.
newsitem.headline: VOTE says NZ Electoral Commission ads misleading.

text.p: The Voters' Organisation for Tactical Education (VOTE) on Wednesday called for the Electoral Commission's advertising to be withdrawn, claiming it was misleading.
VOTE said an advertisement which appeared in the Sunday Star Times of September 1 stating that "the more Party Votes a party gets, the more seats it gets in Parliament" was factually incorrect.
It said latest Colmar Brunton poll figures suggested the governing National Party would win 42 electorate seats or 35 percent in a 120-member parliament.

Assuming a voter turnout of two million, that meant National would need 700,000 votes "just to qualify for the seats they have already won". If it won fewer than 700,000, it would still retain the 42 electorate seats, "making the advertisement incorrect".

It also said that the Electoral Commission's slogan "it takes just two ticks" was over-simplistic, and the logo showing two ticks side by side could be interpreted as supporting the National Party's line.
VOTE filed its complaint with the Advertising Standards Complaints Board on Wednesday morning, with the hope that the advertisements could be withdrawn immediately, "before it's too late".
VOTE says its aim is to educate voters about the MMP system and the opportunities for tactical voting. It refuses to disclose the source of its funding.
